[[Oceania]] is a [[region]] centered on the [[island]]s of the tropical [[Pacific Ocean]].<ref>For a history of the term, see Douglas & Ballard (2008) ''Foreign bodies: Oceania and the science of race 1750–1940''</ref> Conceptions of what constitutes Oceania vary, with it being defined in various ways, often [[geopolitics|geopolitically]] or [[geography|geographically]]. In the geopolitical conception used by the [[United Nations geoscheme|United Nations]], [[International Olympic Committee]], and many atlases, the Oceanic region includes [[Australia]] and the nations of the Pacific from [[Papua New Guinea]] east, but not the [[Malay Archipelago]] or [[Western New Guinea|Indonesian New Guinea]].<ref name="unsd-m49">{{cite web |url=http://millenniumindicators.un.org/unsd/methods/m49/m49regin.htm#oceania |title=United Nations Statistics Division – Countries of Oceania |publisher=Millenniumindicators.un.org |access-date=2009-04-17 |archive-date=2011-07-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713041240/http://millenniumindicators.un.org/unsd/methods/m49/m49regin.htm#oceania |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Atlas of Canada Web Master |url=http://atlas.nrcan.gc.ca/site/english/maps/reference/international/world/referencemap_image_view |title=The Atlas of Canada – The World – Continents |publisher=Atlas.nrcan.gc.ca |date=2004-08-17 |access-date=2009-04-17 |archive-date=2012-11-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104233233/http://atlas.nrcan.gc.ca/site/english/maps/reference/international/world/referencemap_image_view |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.olympic.org/en/content/National-Olympic-Committees/ ''Current IOC members''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091002233312/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/National-Olympic-Committees/ |date=2009-10-02 }}.</ref> The term is sometimes used more specifically to denote Australasia as a geographic [[continent]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mx.encarta.msn.com/encyclopedia_761557382/Ocean%C3%ADa.html |title=Encarta Mexico "Oceanía" |publisher=Mx.encarta.msn.com |access-date=2009-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090317194849/http://mx.encarta.msn.com/encyclopedia_761557382/Ocean%C3%ADa.html |archive-date=2009-03-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Lewis |first=Martin W. |author2=Kären E. Wigen |title=The Myth of Continents: a Critique of Metageography |year=1997 |publisher=University of California Press |location=Berkeley |id={{ISBN|0-520-20743-2}} |page=32 |isbn=0-520-20742-4 |quote= Interestingly enough, the answer [from a scholar who sought to calculate the number of continents] conformed almost precisely to the conventional list: North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Oceania (Australia plus New Zealand), Africa, and Antarctica.}}</ref> 
or biogeographically as a synonym for either the [[Australasian realm]] ([[Wallacea]] and [[Australasia]]) or the [[Oceanian realm]] ([[Melanesia]], [[Polynesia]], and [[Micronesia]] apart either from [[New Zealand]]<ref>Udvardy. 1975. ''A classification of the biogeographical provinces of the world''</ref> or from mainland [[New Guinea]]<ref>Steadman. 2006. ''Extinction & biogeography of tropical Pacific birds''</ref>).

Although [[Christmas Island]] and the [[Cocos (Keeling) Islands]] belong to the Commonwealth of Australia and are inhabited, they are nearer [[Indonesia]] than the Australian mainland, and are commonly associated with [[Asia]] instead of Oceania.

== Notes ==
{{NoteFoot}}

{{Cnote|a|Papua New Guinea has over 860 non-official languages, comprising approximately ten percent of all languages on Earth.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20260118034600/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/papua-new-guinea/ Papua New Guinea], [[CIA World Factbook]]</ref>}}

{{Cnote|b|Melanesian [[pidgin]] is [[lingua franca]] in much of the country, but English remains the official language.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20260114031303/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/solomon-islands/ Solomon Islands], [[CIA World Factbook]]</ref>}}

{{Cnote|c|Samoan and English were declared the official languages of American Samoa in June, 2010, via a constitutional amendment to the 1967 Revised Constitution of American Samoa.<ref name="americansamoa1"/>}}

{{Cnote|d|Palaun is the official language in all islands except [[Sonsoral]] (Sonsoralese and English are official), [[Tobi (island)|Tobi]] (Tobi and English are official), and [[Angaur]] (Angaur, Japanese, and English are official).}}

{{Cnote|e|Based on a 1969 estimate.}}

{{Cnote|f|English, while not an official language, is widely understood, spoken, and used for most government and commercial purposes.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20260115003126/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/nauru/ Nauru], [[CIA World Factbook]]</ref>}}

{{Cnote|g|Norfuk was made the second official language of Norfolk Island in 2005.<ref name="RNZI_16223">{{cite web |url=http://www.rnzi.com/pages/news.php?op=read&id=16223 |title=Norfuk declared official language in Norfolk Island - report |date=April 20, 2005 |work=[[Radio New Zealand International]] |access-date=September 27, 2011}}</ref>}}

{{Cnote|h|While no valid literacy data is available, Norfolk Island is assumed to have an adult literacy rate roughly at a par with Australia's literacy rate of 99%.<ref>[http://erwin.bernhardt.net.nz/oceania/norfolkislandfacts.html Norfolk Island History and Facts in Brief]. Erwin.bernhardt.net.nz. Retrieved on 2010-11-12.</ref>}}

{{Cnote|i|On [[Atafu]], all Congregational Christian Church of Samoa; on [[Nukunonu]], all Roman Catholic; on [[Fakaofo]], both denominations, with the Congregational Christian Church predominant.}}

{{Cnote|j|While no valid literacy data is available, Niue is assumed to have an adult literacy rate of almost 100%.<ref>[http://www.unesco.org/education/wef/countryreports/niue/rapport_2_1.html Niue: Report: Part II: Analytic Sections: cont. 1]. Unesco.org. Retrieved on 2010-11-12.</ref>}}

{{Cnote|k|The Foreign and Commonwealth Office does not hold any statistical information on the literacy rate of the Pitcairn population.<ref>[https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200910/cmhansrd/cm100105/text/100105w0051.htm House of Commons Hansard Written Answers for 05 Jan 2010 (pt 0051)]. Publications.parliament.uk. Retrieved on 2010-11-12.</ref>}}

{{Cnote|l|The residents of the Pitcairn Islands are descendants of [[HMS Bounty]] mutineers<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20260119095311/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/pitcairn-islands/ Pitcairn Islands], [[CIA World Factbook]]</ref> and their Tahitian wives.}}

{{Cnote|m|Much of the information on these two websites is taken from the censuses of other countries, and are not based on independent US government research. The remaining figures are based on estimates, and have been used only where census information from the nation in question is incomplete, unclear, or nonexistent.}}
